Guru: Exactly. Having studied the nine planets in this manner, he imparts this knowledge to humanity. It manifested as Yugas. Which Yugas could they be? The Treta Yuga is calculated by subtracting the duration of Kali Yuga from the Satya Yuga. The Dvapara Yuga is derived by subtracting the duration of Kali from the Treta Yuga. The Kali Yuga comprises four lakh thirty-two thousand (4,32,000) years. This epoch belongs to the Shudra. The prophetic tradition had never attempted to perceive things in such a manner.
Disciple: Did they not attempt to perceive it, or were they unable to attain it?

Guru: They were indeed unable to attain it. When actions unaligned with truth are observed, a conflict arises between the laborer and the capitalist—claiming, "They do not yield all that they acquire. They seek to destroy us." There exists an exploitative class that merely instigates people to fight by propagating such narratives! A class that incites both groups against each other, suggesting that if the capitalist is ruined, the workers will inherit everything! The result: both will be annihilated. The ownership of the karma to destroy both belongs to this class. This is not what is genuinely required. How long is our lifespan? A hundred years at most. Within this span, one must assess the proportion of merit (*punya*) and sin (*papa*) holistically, determining what actions a human should perform at specific times. There is a karma born within the framework of the nine planets, twelve zodiac signs, and twenty-seven constellations. A trajectory was formulated incorporating these twenty-seven constellations, akin to the equator delineated for the Earth. Similar to that imaginary line, this was constructed, and a mathematical system was devised for it. This calculation was conceptualized in India. India's calculation is the most comprehensive. The aforementioned prophets lacked this mathematical insight. Why? Their thirst for inquiry had not reached those depths. This can only be attained by contemplating the underlying causes for the creation of the Earth, the Moon, and so forth. India possesses such a guiding vision derived through this contemplation. There, as previously mentioned, even an insect is accorded a place (compassion). What was the consequence of proceeding with such compassion? The Aryan religion emerged. Various religions were sequentially established. Subsequently, all of this was consolidated to establish Advaita. Madhva attempted to establish Dvaita. All these individuals articulated what they perceived. No matter how long one argues about these matters or emerges victorious in debates, foresight will not simply materialize. Therefore, it is prudent to set that aside. Based on the nine planets, twelve zodiac signs, and twenty-seven constellations, the *Yama* calculation determines what transpires every two and a half to three hours. A certain number of *Yamas* constitute a day; as that calculation becomes infinitesimally smaller, it reaches the fraction of time it takes a healthy human to pierce two stacked tender leaves of a bael tree or lotus with a stylus, penetrating one leaf to reach the other. Identifying that precise moment is the challenge. Then comes the *Mahani* calculation. One thousand *Mahanis* equate to sixty-two and a half *Vinazhikas*. I have studied all this through writing. India possesses a metric of time far more precise than the calculation of a second.
Disciple: Is this not a branch of astrology?
Guru: Astrology is precisely this. Is astrology not entirely based on calculations?
Disciple: However, when calculations are performed currently, they do not seem accurate!
Guru: That is because sufficient effort is not invested to compute them meticulously. One has to dance to the tunes of the world, after all!

Disciple: It is said that such profound calculations were attained! Yet, they are referred to as visionaries who lacked access to such grand metrics. Nevertheless, they did establish a culture here, did they not?

Guru: That is undeniably our own fault. This intellectual alienated us, preventing the Dravidians from uniting, precluding the Shudras from coming together, and thereby keeping people estranged by denying them education. He appropriated it for himself.
Disciple: Who?
Guru: These immigrants. Are they not referred to as those who migrated from the banks of the Sarasvati River?
Guruvani
November 1989

The Aryans were migrants from the Middle East. Upon arriving here and beholding this beautiful land, they established their settlements. Arriving here, they drove away the Konkanis who had previously propagated culture in this region. Consequently, the Konkanis were left with nowhere to reside. Their language was also eradicated. To this day, they lack such a distinct language. The language they do possess lacks a script. Fleeing from here, they migrated to Goa. Unable to sustain themselves there either, they fled from Goa. Thus, they scattered across various locations. In reality, is there a favorable perception of them even today? Are they not still subjected to mockery—through stories and plays? They are unanchored individuals. They continue to wander aimlessly, untouched by stability. Even today, they can only be described as a destitute community. Although they fled once, they returned here, aligned with the Brahmins, constructed the Vedic system, and reverted to becoming Brahmins. Their era has concluded. They failed to respect the changing times. The present epoch belongs to the Shudra.

"Shudra" signifies the ignorant one. The era of the ignorant has arrived. The entirety of these emergent prophets originates from the Shudra class. For instance, is Thiruvalluvar not a member of the *Parayi petta panthirukulam* (the twelve clans born to the Paraiyar woman)? It is such prophets or sages who endure here today. The others have all faded away. Similarly, within the prophetic tradition in the Western world, it was the Shudra from the lowest echelon who emerged from among the fishermen. This serves as yet another testament that the contemporary era belongs to the Shudra.

There is ample evidence that the era of the Brahmanas and Kshatriyas has ended. Who has stated this? It is a description by Manu. The Kshatriyas conquered and ruled here and there, and then abandoned it. Later, it became a system of ruling through plunder. After that, it was handed over to the Shudra - the Pulaya. Who is the Yadava himself? He is from a backward class. The story of such a backward person is spread all over India. Krishna belonged to the avarna class. Krishna is indeed dark-skinned. Isn't the avarna who lives comfortably today very handsome? Thus, good times came for the avarna.

Knowledge was imparted through an ethereal voice that Krishna would be born. The entire capability of this action is the sanctuary of the sages who discover such things. Even though the production nature of medicines discovered without any modern laboratory systems was found and recorded, in which laboratory did the sages discover all this?
Disciple: The growth of their own soul.

Guru: Yes. That growth is what we have lost today. Why was it lost? The Brahmana concealed the truth of Brahmajnana, that knowledge, and placed his Vedic religion before us. That has transformed into today's singing, dancing, and the torch-bearing uncle.

Disciple: Today, a conceptual installation has been established here. The Omkara blooming in a lotus. A human figure standing in position embracing it. I understand this as the form of knowledge awakening in a human being. It means the knowledge that can be awakened in a human. Even so, isn't this an installation? Isn't this also like a temple system? Could you explain the difference between the old temple concept and this?

Guru: A deity has a status and a time. The deity's time is the Treta Yuga and the Dvapara Yuga. At that time, even the sages stood subordinate to the deity. Not enslaved. They would not cross that limit. 'Sreevatsankitavakshasu' - the mark called Sreevatsam is where Sage Bhrigu kicked Mahavishnu. If you ask the reason for kicking, that is another subject. It is understood that this human being possesses so much knowledge, right!
Disciple: Understood.

Guru: So, shouldn't such guides be the ones guiding us? The tradition of a Hindu is like this. There is no such thing as a Hindu. This continent represents the tradition of such a guide, or prophet, or Guru. The aforementioned is proof of that. But he can only communicate up to a certain extent. Why? If you look at the facilities a hundred years ago, how would it be? How far could we travel a hundred years ago? Horses, horse-drawn carriages, and bullock carts. Then one had to walk. Another example - take the names of ancient kings. Their name was 'Vanavaramban'. For a king of that era, traveling that much was sufficient. But today? The distance traveled in an entire lifetime can now be covered in four hours.

Whatever that may be, today we have suffered the misfortune of having to understand the state of the world through intellectuals. In which era are we living? In an era of such immense speed, we have reached a pace where ignorance is proclaimed as knowledge. Two things - one, flying very high in modern terms. We have reached a point where we can travel to another planet. At the same time, scientists are now discovering that traveling so fast between these planets is certainly not beneficial. Why?
Disciple: The speed of creation and the speed of discoveries do not align.

Guru: Yes. There is a sphere existing between the earth, the sun, and the moon, isn't there! That sphere is being ruptured. Because of the desire to travel in that planetary expanse, when traveling there, it goes by piercing this sphere. Through it, a ray will spread here. It should only extend up to a certain point. Or it should remain as it is; that is the concept of the sages. Do not go there. Going there will lead to destruction. Did you observe the distance of the discoveries?
Guruvani
December 1989

Guru: It was Bharadwaja who discovered Vimana Shastra (Bharadwaja Samhita). Bharadwaja's actions illustrate that disobeying a Guru's words will lead to destruction. When he was ready for the practical application of his discovery, the Guru warned him not to do it, stating it would lead to destruction. But Bharadwaja did not obey. He went to Ceylon with an aircraft having bulletproof glass and presented it to Kubera. That concept associated with Ravana came through Kubera. What happened eventually? A woman from the discoverer's own country was abducted in this very aircraft. That became the seed of destruction.
Disciple: Is this a vision?
Guru: This is indeed a vision. But it represents another path.
Disciple: Didn't we receive this information here through a vision?

Guru: No. There is history. Even though the Guru was present and had cautioned him, as a result of the disciple trying to exhibit his brilliance, a part of the country submerged into the sea. The very destruction the Guru had indicated earlier transpired. A portion of the country where the disciple, who ignored the Guru's words, operated went into the sea. The small fraction that remained amounted to nothing. Isn't that how Lanka stands even today? Overall, that kingdom perished. This also serves as a warning that such a truth should not be forgotten. From time to time, nature has been providing us with evidence.

Kubera is one of the great emperors in the world. Kubera's kingdom is near Dwaraka. Because it was associated with actions taken without obeying the Guru, this country also faced destruction. Because a woman was abducted, a curse befell here as well. A war ensued between such individuals.

What did they do subsequently? They wrote the story of the Brahmana. They made the other one a Dravidian. They wrote that he possessed ten heads and many such undesirable things. But if an action to destroy him had not occurred, his (the Dravidian's) ignorance would have amplified. Without abandoning this, he continues as a devotee of Shiva. The intelligent Vaishnava examined history. Then he realized that the era had passed. Thus it became everything in the hands of the one who embraced the Vaishnava concept. Because he wouldn't let go, they began creating the aforementioned Acharyas in this manner. Thinking that at least some dharma should prevail among humanity, Gurus were appointed in various places. Since it wasn't possible to travel so far and reach across a vast sphere back then, temples were established in different locations.
Disciple: Then what about the statement that temples are not needed?

Guru: I did not say that temples are not needed. It means the concept should be transformed. How should the temple be changed? The temple of those days is unnecessary. That follows the Vedic method. That is Tantra. (It is referred to as mantras and tantras - not truth.) Because he didn't claim it as the truth, he did not lie. For instance, a Tantri who is a specific Namboothiri. There too, he collected money without lying. I will demonstrate many tantras to you. You must give me money. And you did give it. You yielded to many things as well. Standing on that support, how many things did he manipulate? They even conducted Devadasi dances inside the temple. Thus, the sanctity of the temple was lost. Even if you adopt the method of the one who installed it, you can only progress up to a certain limit--the underlying principle is different, isn't it!

The deity's status and decorations constitute the aforementioned chaos. How is a Devi temple decorated? If you observe the Madurai Meenakshi temple, you will see that it depicts the commotions of the dance of Shakti and Shiva. Where is the spirituality in that? This is a grand temple, not merely in South India, but in the world itself. Are Hindus capable of imparting any knowledge regarding these commotions?
Disciple: All of that is considered a part of our culture.
Guru: It is indeed culture. Each architectural element within it signifies a particular achievement. All of that is true. But look at how the concept of God we have constructed here is!
Disciple: No one contemplates that, Guru!

Guru: That is correct. Because this ignorance is deeply entrenched within us, we have been unable to attain the realm of true knowledge. Consequently, everything perceived was regarded as God. As the Master observed, 'To them, Yakshis and phantoms are deities. For us, Madan, Marutha, and Bhadrakali are deities. An entity clutching skulls and serpents is our god. To what extent will such a deity benefit us? Did this ferocious manifestation arrive to confer blessings upon us?' It is to such entities that ranks from Durga to Chamundeshwari have been assigned. They have been extolled through nine legendary exploits and woven into mythologies (tales of incarnation). What we have inherited is the residue of the karma enacted through such fabricated narratives. We have remained oblivious to this.

What is this? This is the karma revealed in the visionary realm for the preparation of the Treta and Dvapara Yugas. It is not to say that it does not exist. The Brahmin himself has stated that this is not spirituality. Furthermore, it is an essence formulated in accordance with each individual's level of knowledge. To cultivate that essence, a social structure is necessary. Temples and prayer halls were conceptualized as such social structures. They have not understood any of this at all.
Guruvani
